channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Outlines Steps for Obtaining Kandas Status
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection has detailed the process for obtaining Kandas status, aimed at ethnic Kazakhs returning to the country. The steps include choosing a region, passing a Kazakh language test, completing an application, undergoing state verification, and an interview. Successful applicants may receive relocation subsidies and support for integration.

item.title: Kazakhstan Now Offers Help for Domestic Violence Victims via Threads
item.description: Individuals in Kazakhstan experiencing domestic violence, or those who witness it, can now seek advice from specialists via Threads without needing to report to the police. The Ministry of Internal Affairs has launched a campaign offering legal and psychological support, with a dedicated resource providing contact details for support services nationwide.

item.title: Taliban Ministry Reports 416 Afghan Migrants Returned After Pakistani Prison Release
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Refugees and Repatriation announced that 416 Afghan migrants returned to Afghanistan via the Torkham border crossing after being released from Pakistani prisons. This follows Pakistan's intensified arrests and deportations of undocumented Afghan migrants.

item.title: Turkmenistan Halts Foreign Parcel Deliveries After Tramadol Discovery
item.description: Turkmenistan has suspended the delivery of foreign parcels for about a week following the discovery of a large shipment of tramadol, an opioid analgesic banned in the country. Customs reportedly intercepted the shipment in late October, possibly from Turkey.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister to Attend AI Security Summit in Astana
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Jeyenbek Kulubaev, will participate in the "Aqaba Process" summit on artificial intelligence security in Astana on November 6. The summit, initiated by the presidents of Kazakhstan and Jordan, will discuss international security related to AI development and use.

item.title: UN clears over 72,000 square meters of explosive remnants in Afghanistan
item.description: The UN Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan (UN-STFA) announced the clearance of over 72,000 square meters of land contaminated with explosive remnants of war in Kunduz and Baghlan provinces. The operation also included educating families about the dangers.

item.title: Kazakhstan banks increasingly favor business lending over consumer loans, says National Bank
item.description: Banks in Kazakhstan are now more inclined to issue loans to businesses than to individuals, according to the National Bank. This shift is attributed to government measures, including differentiated taxation, aimed at stimulating corporate lending.

item.title: Eight Officials Arrested in Kazakhstan Caspian Sea Military Deaths Case
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office announced the arrest of eight officials in connection with the deaths of servicemen during Caspian Sea exercises. Investigations are nearing completion, with over 300 individuals interviewed and more than 30 expert examinations conducted. The accused face charges of negligence and violating navigation rules.

item.title: Former Kazakh Official Sentenced to 10 Years for Taking Bribes to Facilitate Truck Crossings
item.description: A former acting head of a state revenue department in West Kazakhstan region has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for accepting bribes totaling 100 million tenge. He facilitated the passage of over 1,000 Russian trucks by bypassing risk management systems. An accomplice who acted as a mediator received a 1.5-year sentence.

item.title: Water supply and treatment systems launched in 70 settlements across Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Water supply and purification systems have been successfully launched in 70 populated areas throughout Kyrgyzstan. This initiative aims to improve access to clean water and sanitation for numerous communities across the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan army to adopt 6+6 model for military service reform
item.description: Kazakhstan's army will change its conscription system, dividing the 12-month service into two six-month phases. The first phase will focus on training in educational centers, while the second will involve service in military units, aiming to enhance combat readiness and civilian skills.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Allocate $2.5 Million for New Bridge Construction at Turkmenistan Border
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has ordered the allocation of 25 billion Uzbek soums (approximately $2.5 million) for the construction of a new bridge and road infrastructure in the Alot district. The current bridge, built around 1980, is insufficient for the growing transport needs. The new modern concrete bridge will serve the border trade zone and logistics center.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China Agree to Increase Weekly Flights and Add New Destinations
item.description: Kazakhstan and China have agreed to increase the number of authorized flights between the two countries from 150 to 180 per week. Additionally, the cities of Chengdu and Kashgar will be added to the route network. These agreements were reached during a civil aviation cooperation conference in Tashkent.

item.title: Former West Kazakhstan Official Sentenced to 10 Years for Accepting 100 Million Tenge Bribe
item.description: A former acting head of a department in the West Kazakhstan regional state revenue committee has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for accepting a bribe of 100 million tenge. He facilitated the passage of 1,003 trucks from Russia. A Russian citizen involved in the scheme received 1.5 years for mediation.

item.title: Tajikistan's Minister of Transport Inspects Baljuvon-Sari Khosor Road Reconstruction
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Transport, Azim Ibrahim, visited the first phase of the Baljuvon-Sari Khosor road reconstruction. The project involves 115 workers, including 40 Chinese nationals and 75 locals. The 54.1 km road will feature 10 bridges and 121 culverts, funded by the EBRD and built by a Chinese company.

item.title: Kyrgyz Citizen Accused of Large-Scale Fraud Extradited from Georgia
item.description: A Kyrgyz citizen, identified by initials M. Zh., has been extradited from Georgia to Kyrgyzstan to face charges of large-scale fraud. He allegedly defrauded a victim by falsely promising to sell a car. The suspect fled abroad to evade prosecution. The General Prosecutor's Office is continuing efforts to locate and return fugitives.

item.title: Former Turkic Council Chief Criticizes Kazakhstan's Proposal to Include Russia in OTG+
item.description: Khalil Akıncı, former Secretary General of the Turkic Council, expressed surprise at Kazakhstan's President Tokayev's proposal to invite Russia into the Organization of Turkic States (OTG) format. Akıncı believes such initiatives should be discussed internally first and doubts the proposal will be supported by other members.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Inflation to Continue Slowing in 2027 Despite 'People's Construction' Program, Says National Bank
item.description: Kazakhstan's inflation is expected to continue its gradual slowdown in 2027, even with the economic boost from the 'People's Construction' program, according to the National Bank. The bank has raised its 2027 inflation forecast to 6.5-8.5% from 5.5-7.5% to account for these factors, but still anticipates a downward trend. The goal is to keep inflation near 5%.

item.title: Kazakhstan Economist Downplays Impact of Minimum Wage Hike
item.description: An economist suggests the impact of Kazakhstan's minimum wage increase from 85,000 to 110,000 tenge is overestimated. While it will benefit 1.8 million people, primarily state employees and individual entrepreneurs whose mandatory payments are tied to the minimum wage, private sector wages are linked to inflation, not the minimum wage. Therefore, a significant price increase is not expected.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Over 300 Questioned in Deadly Naval Exercise Investigation
item.description: An investigation into the deaths of 14 naval cadets during exercises in the Caspian Sea is ongoing, with over 300 individuals questioned. Eight officials have been detained on suspicion of negligence and violating navigation rules. The Prosecutor General's Office is closely monitoring the investigation, which is expected to conclude soon. The incident led to a significant public outcry and a reshuffling of the defense ministry leadership.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan to Expand Trade and Security Cooperation in Border Regions
item.description: Officials from Kyrgyzstan's Batken region and Tajikistan's Sughd region met to discuss expanding trade, strengthening border security, and fostering neighborly relations. The Kyrgyz ambassador to Tajikistan emphasized the importance of stable ties and expressed confidence in developing new areas of cooperation between the two countries and their border areas.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Oil Reserves Estimated at 785 Million Tons, Sufficient for Decades
item.description: The chairman of KazMunayGaz, Kazakhstan's national oil and gas company, has estimated the country's oil reserves at 785 million tons. This substantial reserve is expected to meet the nation's needs for many years to come, ensuring continued energy production and export capabilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan to Increase Air Flights Between Cities
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have agreed to increase the number of flights on the Almaty-Tashkent and Astana-Tashkent routes to 60 per week. Other routes between the two countries will see weekly flights rise from 14 to 20. The agreement was reached during talks in Tashkent.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Rules for Military Service Deferrals and Exemptions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense has introduced new regulations concerning military service deferrals and the issuance of military ID cards. The updated rules specify criteria for deferment or exemption, including care for family members, single parenthood, and raising dependents for at least two years.

item.title: US Midterm Elections: Old Patterns, New Trends, and Impact on Central Asia
item.description: Political analyst Dosym Satpayev examines the US midterm elections, noting historical patterns of presidential party losses in Congress. He discusses the factors influencing voter behavior, including economic dissatisfaction and political mobilization, and considers potential implications for Central Asia.

item.title: Aktobe-Kandyagash Road Section in Kazakhstan to Become Toll Road
item.description: A section of the Aktobe-Kandyagash highway in Kazakhstan, from kilometer 11 to 100, will become a toll road. The Ministry of Transport announced that the payment system will be differentiated, with all vehicles paying on the 11-87 km stretch and only buses and trucks on the 87-100 km section. Funds will support road maintenance.

item.title: Trump Admits Iran War Affected Republican Midterm Election Performance
item.description: US President Donald Trump acknowledged that the war with Iran influenced the Republican Party's performance in the midterm elections. Despite this, he defended his decision to pursue the conflict, stating it was necessary to prevent Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon. The war has been cited as a factor in rising petrol prices.

item.title: Investigation Nears Completion in Deadly Caspian Military Exercise Incident
item.description: An investigation into the deaths of military personnel during a training exercise in the Caspian Sea is nearing completion. Over 300 individuals have been questioned, and more than 30 expert examinations have been conducted. Eight officials, including high-ranking naval commanders, have been detained on suspicion of negligence and violating navigation rules. The Prosecutor General's Office is closely monitoring the investigation.

item.title: Uzbek President Aims for 1 Million Tons of Cotton in Bukhara Within Three Years
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reclaim 100,000 hectares of desert land in the Bukhara region for cotton and wheat cultivation and orchard development. President Mirziyoyev announced a goal to produce 1 million tons of cotton in Bukhara within three years, significantly increasing the current target. He also noted that Uzbekistan has harvested nearly 5 million tons of cotton this year.

item.title: Netanyahu Labels Arab Israeli Parties as Hamas Supporters, Warns Against Their Government Inclusion
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has characterized Arab Israeli parties as supporters of Hamas and cautioned against their potential entry into the Israeli government, stating it would lead to the country's collapse. Arab Israeli parties secured a record 19 seats in the recent parliamentary elections, while Netanyahu's rival considers forming a coalition with them.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Oil and Gas Companies Prevented from Illegal Gas Sales
item.description: Uzbekistan's "O'zenergoinspeksiya" reported that 15 oil and gas companies in the country are under strict control. These companies cannot illegally sell gas to neighboring countries or other regions, as their operations are closely monitored. The agency emphasized that there is no possibility of illicit product diversion.

item.title: Tajikistan and Egypt Discuss Cooperation in Innovation and AI
item.description: Representatives from Tajikistan's Agency of Innovation and Digital Technologies met with Egyptian businessman Odil Donish to discuss cooperation in innovation, digital technologies, and artificial intelligence. They explored investment opportunities, joint initiatives, and the exchange of experience in developing tech parks and IT companies. Egypt's Smart Villages and Silicon Waha experience may be used for Tajikistan's digital infrastructure.

item.title: Investigation into Deaths of 14 Soldiers in Kazakhstan Nears Completion
item.description: The military investigation into the deaths of 14 soldiers in Kazakhstan's Mangystau region is nearing its conclusion. Over 300 people have been interviewed, and more than 30 forensic examinations have been conducted. The General Prosecutor's Office stated that all circumstances of the tragic incident have been thoroughly and objectively established. The investigation is expected to conclude soon.

item.title: Why is Waste Recycling Lagging in Kazakhstan Despite Significant Funding?
item.description: Despite billions of tenge allocated and new enterprises opened, waste recycling in Kazakhstan remains underdeveloped, with much waste still landfilled. Even separately collected waste is sometimes mixed. An expert from the "Baitak" Green Party explains the slow progress and the effectiveness of state support in addressing these issues. Official data shows 15 projects operational, processing 290,000 tons annually.

item.title: Over 300 Questioned in Investigation of Servicemembers' Deaths in Mangistau
item.description: The investigation into the deaths of servicemen during exercises in Kazakhstan's Mangistau region continues. Over 300 people have been questioned, and more than 30 forensic examinations have been conducted. Eight officials, suspected of negligence and violating navigation rules, have been detained.

item.title: Taliban Begin Gold Extraction Operations in Panjshir Province
item.description: The Taliban have reportedly commenced gold extraction activities in the Panjshir province of Afghanistan. This development marks a new phase in the region's economic activities under Taliban control, focusing on natural resource exploitation.

item.title: Turkey's Ruling Party Official: Russia Does Not Meet Observer Status Requirements for Turkic States Organization
item.description: Kurshad Zorlu, deputy chairman of Turkey's ruling party, stated that Russia does not meet the requirements to become an observer in the Organization of Turkic States. He emphasized the need to consider the organization's strategic goals and the common interests of the Turkic world. The statement came in response to Russia's request for observer status.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans $350 Million Data Center and Solar Power Plant in Bukhara
item.description: A $350 million data center is planned for the Olot district of Bukhara region, Uzbekistan. Foreign investors have purchased 90 hectares for the project, which is expected to create 300 permanent jobs. Details on investors, land terms, and completion dates were not disclosed. A solar power plant is also part of the development.

item.title: US Imposes Sanctions on Tajik National for Alleged Assistance to Iran
item.description: The United States has imposed sanctions on Alisher Domullojanov, a Russian and Tajik citizen born in Dushanbe, for allegedly attempting to procure portable anti-aircraft missile systems for Iran. The sanctions, part of a broader effort to curb Iran's arms procurement, also target companies involved in facilitating these transfers.

item.title: South Korea Plans to Extend Naval Mission to Waters Near Strait of Hormuz
item.description: South Korea intends to expand its anti-piracy mission from off the coast of Somalia to waters near the Strait of Hormuz. The move, requiring parliamentary approval, aims to support efforts to restore freedom of navigation in the strategic waterway, with operations limited to international waters south of Oman.
